summary: Tailwind plugin fetches and eval()s remote JavaScript on build
details: sw-pluginer presents itself as a Tailwind service-worker plugin, but when Tailwind loads the plugin it reads a URL from node_modules/.bin/manifest.json, HTTP-GETs the response body, and passes it directly to eval() inside generateRegistration. Any JavaScript served from that URL executes inside the developer's Node build process. The URL is sourced from a manifest file under node_modules/.bin/, a path a companion or second-stage package can plant, so the fetch target is attacker-controllable and not pinned to any publisher. A doc comment immediately above the eval call states 'safe, no eval', contradicting the code and consistent with deliberate cover-story framing rather than a mistake. Tailwind plugin loading does not require downloading or executing remote JavaScript on the build host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
